title: XRP Price Scenarios as XRP’s Weekly RSI Tests 20 Again
body: XRP’s weekly RSI is testing 20 again after a brief rebound. With XRP near $0.95, the weekly close could help distinguish a second momentum low from further weakness. XRP ’s weekly relative strength index has returned to the 20 area soon after recovering from below it. EGRAG Crypto highlighted the speed of that second test. In earlier cycles, XRP’s weekly momentum had more time to recover after crossing back above 20. This time, the rebound stalled just above the threshold while XRP was still trading below $1. XRP traded at $0.9530 on Bitstamp at 08:08 UTC on November 16, down 2.11% from the previous weekly close. The new week had opened at $0.97361 and traded between $0.94853 and $0.97411. With more than six days left in the candle, both the price and the weekly RSI reading were still provisional. Why XRP’s Second RSI Test Matters Weekly RSI compares the size of recent weekly gains with recent weekly losses on a scale from zero to 100. Traders commonly use 30 as the oversold threshold. EGRAG’s framework uses 20, a more extreme reading that requires losses to outweigh gains by a wider margin. XRP/USD on Bitstamp at 08:08 UTC on November 16. The lower panel highlights weekly RSI’s return to 20, while the upper panel traces a possible W and a falling wedge. The recent sequence unfolded in three stages. First, XRP’s weekly RSI fell below the pink line at 20 and spent time in the low teens. It then recovered into the mid-20s before turning back toward 20. That brief rebound stands apart from the recovery after the 2022 trough, when RSI climbed away from 20 and eventually moved above the midpoint at 50. Deeply oversold readings have occurred before. What EGRAG considers unusual in this cycle is how quickly the first recovery gave way. A second trough near 20 could form the right side of a W in momentum. A weekly close back above 20 would be an initial sign of stabilization. A subsequent push above the intervening peak in the mid-20s would give that interpretation more weight. Conversely, repeated weekly closes below 20 would leave XRP vulnerable to another test of the earlier RSI low. Either outcome concerns the strength of the decline. A price bottom would require separate evidence, as in the earlier XRP daily double-bottom setup near $1 . How the RSI Retest Fits the Green and Blue XRP Scenarios EGRAG’s Team Green interpretation covers several years of XRP price history. Two broad, rounded troughs form a possible W beneath a horizontal boundary near $2.72. At $0.9530, XRP was still far below that boundary. Even a successful weekly RSI rebound would leave considerable distance before price could challenge it. Team Blue focuses on the decline from the 2025 highs. Two descending blue lines connect successively lower highs and lows, narrowing into a possible falling wedge. Under that interpretation, the first price signal would be a break above the wedge’s upper edge. The blue projection extends toward $13 only after an upside breakout. The RSI reading itself supplies no such target. For the nearer term, XRP’s decline alongside the broader crypto market leaves two developments to watch independently: whether weekly RSI can hold 20 and clear its recent rebound high, and whether XRP can break the sequence of lower price highs inside the wedge. The first would mark improving momentum. The second would give that improvement a visible counterpart in price.

title: Amazon Stock: AWS Strikes $5B Blackstone Data Center Deal as AI Spending Grows
body: Key takeaways Amazon and Blackstone agree on $5B data center deal AWS retains minority stake and long-term leasing rights Transaction highlights growing pressure from AI infrastructure spending Amazon ( NASDAQ: AMZN ) has struck a $5 billion data center agreement with Blackstone, bringing outside capital into its cloud infrastructure as the company accelerates artificial intelligence spending and confronts mounting pressure on free cash flow. Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (NYSE: BXDC) announced November 16 that it will acquire approximately 75% of two joint ventures holding 13 newly constructed data centers. Amazon Web Services will retain roughly 25% ownership while leasing back the entire portfolio. The transaction comes after Amazon's AI spending surge pushed its trailing annual free cash flow to negative $42.4 billion, raising questions about how technology companies finance increasingly expensive computing infrastructure. Amazon and Blackstone Structure $5B Data Center Partnership According to Blackstone's official announcement , the transaction covers 13 data center buildings across two AWS campuses in northern Indiana and Mississippi. The facilities provide a combined 647 megawatts of information technology power capacity, including nine buildings in Indiana and four in Mississippi. AWS will lease 100% of the properties under triple-net agreements, with an initial term of 12 years and extension options reaching 32 years. Annual rent increases are set at 2.75%. Blackstone's SEC filing reveals that the financing includes approximately $1.9 billion from its IPO proceeds and $2.5 billion in new property-backed mortgage loans. The $5 billion figure represents the portfolio's aggregate valuation rather than Blackstone's direct cash investment. The deal resembles the broader AI infrastructure financing models emerging across cloud computing, where institutional investors own physical facilities while technology companies retain operational access. AWS Growth Accelerates as Amazon Faces $220B Spending Plan Amazon's latest financial results help explain the transaction's timing. According to its third-quarter earnings release , AWS revenue increased 39% year over year to approximately $46 billion, while operating income reached $17.8 billion. Despite that growth, Amazon expects roughly $220 billion in capital expenditures during 2026, reflecting substantial investment in AI servers, data centers and supporting infrastructure. The company's growing custom AI chip business is another major component of its infrastructure expansion. Amazon has also explored GPU sale-leaseback financing , highlighting how external capital could support computing investments without requiring Amazon to directly own every asset. The Blackstone agreement formalizes that approach for physical data center properties.

title: MSTR Stock: Strategy Buys 485 Bitcoin but Spends $228M on Preferred Share Buybacks
body: Key takeaways Strategy purchases 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million STRC preferred share buybacks reach $228.1 million MSTR stock sales fund purchases and repurchases Michael Saylor's Strategy (NASDAQ: MSTR) purchased another 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million last week, but directed almost seven times that amount toward repurchasing its own preferred shares, highlighting the company's increasingly complex approach to managing its Bitcoin treasury. According to its November 16 SEC filing , Strategy acquired Bitcoin between November 9 and November 15 at an average price of $68,887 per coin. During the same period, it spent $228.1 million buying back 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred stock. The transactions extend a pattern highlighted in Strategy's previous Bitcoin purchase , when preferred stock repurchases also exceeded cryptocurrency acquisitions. Strategy Holds 850,849 Bitcoin After Latest Purchase Strategy's Bitcoin holdings increased to 850,849 BTC as of November 15, representing more than 4% of Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million coins. The company has spent approximately $64.20 billion accumulating those holdings, at an average acquisition price of $75,452 per Bitcoin, including fees and expenses. Its newest purchase came at a substantially lower price than its overall cost basis, reflecting the recent cryptocurrency market downturn. Strategy financed the acquisition through its at-the-market equity offering program, selling 2,087,040 MSTR common shares for $244.7 million in net proceeds. Of that amount, $33.4 million funded Bitcoin purchases, while $206.3 million went toward STRC repurchases and another $5 million was allocated to USD Cash. The financing structure differs from earlier periods when Strategy used a combination of MSTR share sales and cash to accumulate cryptocurrency. Why Is Strategy Spending More on STRC Than Bitcoin? Strategy repurchased $228.1 million worth of STRC shares, using $206.3 million from common stock sales and $21.8 million in interest earned on cash and short-term investments. The buybacks form part of its expanded preferred securities repurchase program , designed to support STRC trading near its $100 stated amount. Strategy maintained STRC's annual dividend rate at 12% for December, while management continues seeking sustained trading near that benchmark. Repurchasing preferred shares can reduce outstanding dividend obligations and potentially strengthen investor confidence in the company's securities. Strategy's broader digital credit framework combines preferred stock, dollar reserves and Bitcoin accumulation rather than focusing exclusively on purchasing more BTC. What Does This Mean for MSTR Stock? Strategy reported a $4.75 billion USD Reserve and $151.2 million in additional USD Cash as of November 15. It also used $18.9 million from its reserve to pay preferred dividends during the reporting week. The company retained $332.2 million under its preferred securities repurchase authorization and $1 billion under its separate MSTR buyback program. Importantly, the latest filing reports no MSTR common-share repurchases. Instead, Strategy issued common shares while buying back STRC preferred stock, potentially increasing the number of common shares outstanding. That distinction reinforces concerns previously examined during Strategy's earlier STRC buybacks .

title: Chartist to XRP Holders: This Is How Bear Markets End. Here’s the Signal
body: A rarely discussed on-chain metric has just reached a record level for XRP. The last time it looked like this, the market was at or near a bottom. Blockchain Backer (@BCBacker), a prominent XRP-focused analyst and content creator, published a post highlighting a striking development in XRP’s on-chain data. The total supply of XRP currently held at a loss has reached 45.1 billion coins, surpassing the previous record of 45.0 billion. He stated, “This isn’t how bear markets start. This is how they’ve ended.” The thing XRP does have going for it here is that this isn't how bear markets start. This is how they've ended. Total coins in a loss: 45.1 b Previous record: 45.0 b These are levels experienced during 2018 capitulation, Covid, SEC lawsuit, 2022 capitulation and the FTX crash. https://t.co/zDBl3e0Zmi pic.twitter.com/PQDMwOJJd7 — Blockchain Backer (@BCBacker) November 15, 2026 What the Metric Measures The “Total Supply in Loss”metric tracks the number of coins last moved at a price higher than the current price. When this number is elevated, it means a large portion of the circulating supply is underwater . Holders who bought at higher prices now hold coins worth less than what they paid. At the time of the data, XRP’s price stood at $0.91. The Historical Context Blockchain Backer’s post identifies the specific market events where this metric previously reached comparable levels. Those events include the 2018 capitulation, the Covid crash, the SEC lawsuit against Ripple , the 2022 capitulation, and the FTX collapse. Each of those moments represented a period of extreme selling pressure and fear. Each was followed by a price recovery. The chart shows this pattern clearly. The green line representing total supply in loss spiked dramatically during each of those events. The current spike now exceeds every prior one on record. Reading the Chart For most of XRP’s history, the total supply in loss fluctuated significantly. During the 2017 bull run, the metric dropped sharply as holders moved into profit. It spiked again as prices collapsed. The same pattern repeated in 2019-2021, and 2024-2025. The current reading of 45.1 billion XRP in loss sits above the dotted horizontal line marking the previous all-time high. This is a new extreme, coming just as XRP hit its lowest price in two years . Why Analysts Are Watching When a record number of holders are sitting at a loss, selling pressure can be intense . But it also signals exhaustion. Sellers who wanted to exit have largely done so. The supply has transferred to new holders at lower prices. Historically, this combination has preceded recoveries rather than further declines. Blockchain Backer’s post does not predict a specific price target. It draws a comparison between current conditions and past capitulation events, all of which preceded meaningful recoveries for XRP. title: Is Wall Street Turning Towards Solana? A Noteworthy Statement from the NYSE!
body: While Bitcoin and altcoins have been facing a downward trend in recent days, a notable development has occurred regarding Solana, one of the established altcoins. Accordingly, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), is preparing to take a significant step towards the Solana ecosystem. ICE Clear Europe President Hester Serafini announced that the NYSE’s alternative trading platform is being prepared to accept tokens issued on Solana. NYSE Opens the Door to Tokens on Solana! In a video released by Solana on November 16, Hester Serafini, Head of ICE Clear Europe, stated that the New York Stock Exchange’s alternative trading system, ATS, is ready to accept tokens created on the Solana network. This announcement suggests that the integration between traditional financial markets and blockchain technology could be taken to a new level. ICE Could Be a Validator in the Solana Network! Another important detail in Serafini’s statement was that ICE is considering the possibility of becoming a validator on the Solana network. Serafini stated that ICE Digital Trust already supports Solana and that the company is examining the option of acting as a validator on the network. Implementing such a step could mean that traditional financial infrastructure directly contributes to the security and transaction verification processes of the Solana network. On the other hand, it was recently announced that the NYSE is considering Avalanche for its clearing and ledger infrastructure in its planned digital securities platform. This development reveals that traditional financial institutions are evaluating different blockchain networks in their tokenization processes. These steps towards Solana and Avalanche indicate that the use of blockchain technologies in the corporate finance world may expand. In conclusion, ICE’s consideration of becoming a validator on Solana and NYSE ATS’s preparation to accept Solana-based tokens are significant developments that could strengthen the network’s position in the institutional finance world. However, it should be noted that these statements do not yet represent a completed integration or a finalized validator decision. *This is not investment advice. title: Strategy buys 485 BTC after MSCI cut as Strive lifts buy to 251
body: Strategy (NASDAQ: MSTR) and Strive (NASDAQ: ASST), two of the most consistent corporate Bitcoin buyers, disclosed in their latest SEC filings on Monday, November 16, that they bought 485 and 251 Bitcoin, respectively. The 485 BTC purchase announced by Michael Saylor’s Strategy is the firm’s first reported buy since MSCI’s November 11 confirmation that it would drop the company’s stock. How much did Strategy spend on Bitcoin last week? Saylor’s leading Bitcoin accumulator, Strategy, spent $33.4 million on the 485 BTC it bought, according to its 8-K filing for the period between November 9 and November 15. It paid an average of $68,887 per token. Excerpt from Strategy’s SEC 8-K filing. Source: SEC The updated figures on Strategy’s entire Bitcoin stash as of November 16 are now at 850,849 BTC, bought at an average price of $75,452 per token. The entire stockpile cost $64.20 billion to build. The firm now holds more than 4% of Bitcoin’s 21-million supply cap. The 1,036 Bitcoin purchase Strategy disclosed one week ago is more than double this week’s 485 BTC. Strategy spent more on STRC buybacks Strategy’s spending on buying back its own STRC preferred shares was the bigger headline, with the $228.1 million spent to repurchase 2.28 million units of STRC amounting to almost seven times the roughly $33 million the firm spent on Bitcoin. The week’s spending was funded by the $244.7 million Strategy raised from 2.09 million MSTR common shares sales. $33.4 million of the raise went to Bitcoin, STRC buybacks got $206.3 million of the raise and $5 million went to cash. The remaining $21.8 million of the STRC repurchase came from interest income. Strategy said it would hold the STRC dividend at 12% through December record dates until the shares trade steadily near $100. As of November 15, its US dollar reserve stood at $4.75 billion, with a separate cash balance of $151.2 million. How much did Strive spend on Bitcoin last week? Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole of the Dallas-based Bitcoin treasury firm Strive said the company spent $17.5 million on 251 BTC at an average price of $69,853. Strive now has 43,404 BTC in its corporate treasury. The 251 Bitcoin purchase week is a sharp acceleration from the 29 BTC the firm bought the week before. The funds came from $10 million through Strive’s SATS at-the-market program, selling 104,478 shares of its 15% Series A perpetual preferred stock and no common shares. Cash fell $22.3 million to $465.3 million as of November 13. Strive still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred, marked at $50.5 million. MSCI to remove Strategy on November 30 MSCI has confirmed that it will cut Strategy from its USA Index and Metaplanet from its Japan Small Cap Index at the close of business on November 30, following a review published last week. The move stems from new rules excluding “non-operating” firms whose digital-asset holdings make up at least half of total assets. Strategy’s filing shows passive funds tracking MSCI indexes hold nearly $3 billion in MSTR, more than 3% of its shares. JPMorgan has estimated outflows could reach $8.8 billion if other providers follow. Saylor and President Phong Le previously called the treatment of digital-asset treasuries “discriminatory.” Both companies pushed back against MSCI’s eligibility rules. In a December 2025 letter to MSCI, Cole called a 50% Bitcoin threshold “unworkable” and urged the index provider to “let the market decide.” The selling pressure showed up Monday. MSTR fell about 8% in premarket trading from a November 13 close of $111.62, while Strive’s Class A shares dropped roughly 10% to $19.34, tracking a broad slide in Bitcoin-linked stocks after BTC fell below $62,000 over the weekend. title: Market Brief: Bitcoin Falls For 6 Straight Weeks; Rebound Or More Pain Ahead?
body: Summary The bigger problem for Bitcoin is the lack of fresh buying demand to absorb the ongoing selling. Four indicators help explain why. On November 13 and 14, roughly $2.93B worth of crypto long positions were liquidated. Each round of forced selling pushed prices lower, putting the next group of leveraged positions at risk. Could Bitcoin fall further, and would that mean the previous bear market never really ended? Three signals are worth watching. Bitcoin fell to nearly $62K over the weekend, its lowest price since July. BTC has now closed lower for six straight weeks, while ETH and other major cryptocurrencies have also taken heavy losses. Almost $3B in leveraged long positions were liquidated across the crypto market on November 13 and 14. No single event clearly explains the weekend crash. Weak buying demand, tighter liquidity, and leveraged liquidations may have all played a part. With Bitcoin down for six straight weeks, what’s behind the selling, and where could the market go from here? Several Factors May Be Behind the Weekend Selloff 1. Weakening Buying Demand and Shrinking Liquidity The bigger problem for Bitcoin (⁠ BTC-USD ) is the lack of fresh buying demand to absorb the ongoing selling. Four indicators help explain why: ETF Outflows: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.91B over seven consecutive trading days through November 13. Investors have been pulling money out of Bitcoin funds rather than adding to their positions. Stablecoin Supply: The combined supply of USDT, USDC, and DAI fell by $11.5B over the past 30 days, the largest decline in Coinbase Institutional’s dataset. Even after the TerraUSD collapse in May 2022, a major black swan event for crypto, the same measure fell by only $9.2B. Spot CVD: Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) measures the running difference between market buy and sell volume. During Bitcoin’s latest drop, both spot and futures CVD moved sharply lower. More traders were hitting bids than lifting offers, with sellers taking the initiative in both markets. Coinbase Premium: The Coinbase Premium Index offers a view of U.S. spot demand. It has traded below zero for much of the period since May, suggesting that selling pressure has generally outweighed buying interest in the U.S. market. Its 30-day average stands at -0.14%, with 54 consecutive days in negative territory. 2. Macro Pressure and Weakness in AI Stocks Last week’s hotter U.S. inflation data added to concerns about further Fed rate hikes. By November 13, futures markets were pricing in 64 basis points of rate increases over the next 12 months, compared with 37 basis points at the start of November. AI and semiconductor stocks, including Nvidia (⁠ NVDA ), have also been under pressure. Tom Lee suggested that losses in these stocks may have triggered margin calls, forcing some investors to sell crypto to raise cash. He also raised the possibility that investors are selling other assets ahead of Anthropic’s (⁠ ANT ) IPO to free up funds for the offering. 3. Large Liquidations Accelerated the Selloff Bitcoin slipped through $68K, falling below its 200-week moving average. That left leveraged longs exposed to further losses. On November 13 and 14, roughly $2.93B worth of crypto long positions were liquidated. Each round of forced selling pushed prices lower, putting the next group of leveraged positions at risk. With fewer orders on the books over the weekend, even relatively small additional sell orders could move prices more sharply. Similar Bitcoin Selloffs in the Past 6 consecutive weekly losses are unusual for Bitcoin, but we’ve seen this before. 2 recent examples are early 2026 and 2022. Early 2026: BTC lost nearly 30% before bouncing 25% over the next ten weeks. But that wasn’t the bottom. Another seven weeks of selling took Bitcoin down 30% to a new low near $57K. 2022: In 2022, Bitcoin lost nearly 42% in eight weeks. Prices then moved sideways for a short period before plunging another 41%. A 32% rebound followed over the next five weeks, but BTC later fell another 38%, reaching its cycle low near $15.4K in November. In the current downturn, Bitcoin has fallen nearly 29% from its late September high near $87K to around $62K over the weekend. What began as a gradual decline has accelerated sharply in recent days. Could Bitcoin fall further, and would that mean the previous bear market never really ended? Three signals are worth watching: Capital Flows: Watch whether ETF outflows slow down or turn positive. Stablecoin supply also needs to stop shrinking if liquidity is going to improve. Spot Demand: A rising Spot CVD would show buyers becoming more aggressive. A Coinbase Premium moving back above zero would also point to stronger U.S. demand. Price Levels: BTC fell as low as $62K over the weekend, making that the first price level to watch if selling continues. On a rebound, the 200-week moving average near $68K could become resistance. For any rebound to hold, Bitcoin needs buyers to return. Otherwise, another selloff remains a real possibility. title: EU Hits 50 Russian Banks and Oil Export Networks With New Sanctions
body: Key takeaways EU targets nearly 50 Russian financial institutions New sanctions expand pressure on Russian oil exports Brussels adds 113 individuals and entities to restrictions The European Union imposed new sanctions on nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions on November 16, expanding restrictions on Moscow's oil export networks, overseas trading intermediaries and companies supporting its war in Ukraine. The measures add 113 targets to the EU's sanctions lists, including 12 individuals and 101 entities. They cover financial institutions, energy companies and businesses linked to Russia's shadow fleet of oil tankers. According to the European Council's official announcement , the restrictions are designed to reduce Russia's access to financing and revenues supporting its military operations. EU Sanctions Nearly 50 Russian Banks and Financial Firms The latest measures expand the EU's campaign against financial institutions involved in processing transactions and supporting Russian government revenues. Nearly 50 banks and financial organizations appear among the newly designated entities, widening the restrictions introduced through the EU's earlier 21st Russia sanctions package . Under the latest listings, designated entities face asset freezes, while EU individuals and businesses are prohibited from making funds or economic resources available to them. The rules also impose travel restrictions on the listed individuals. Importantly, these measures are not equivalent to a new blanket ban on every Russian bank or an automatic exclusion from the SWIFT financial messaging network. The move comes as Russian financial institutions increasingly explore alternative international payment arrangements, including regulated cryptocurrency settlements . However, the November 16 announcement does not establish new sanctions against a specific cryptocurrency or stablecoin. Russian Oil Exports and Shadow Fleet Face Fresh Restrictions Energy businesses are another major focus of the EU's decision. The Council designated companies involved in managing Russian refineries and the St. Petersburg oil terminal, alongside businesses operating in oil exploration and production. The sanctions also cover companies in China, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Seychelles identified by the Council as purchasers of Russian-origin crude oil products or participants in networks supporting restricted maritime trade. Additional individuals connected to vessels accused of transporting Russian oil in violation of restrictions were also listed. These actions extend existing pressure on Russia's oil trade , which has faced increasing restrictions from Western governments. The immediate impact on global oil prices remains uncertain because the new listings do not automatically remove a measurable quantity of crude from international markets. Why the New Sanctions Matter for Crypto and Global Trade The financial restrictions could increase compliance challenges for businesses processing international payments connected to designated Russian entities. Previous enforcement actions have already targeted Russia-linked shadow banking networks allegedly facilitating cross-border transactions outside conventional channels. U.S. authorities have separately investigated cryptocurrency platforms over suspected Russian sanctions-evasion transactions , underscoring the wider regulatory focus on alternative payment infrastructure. However, today's EU decision specifically concerns newly designated individuals and entities rather than a general prohibition on cryptocurrency payments.

title: BTC May Wander the Wilderness a While Longer, Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan Warns
body: Three Things to Know Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan said crypto feels like mid-2018, when exhausted investors gave up on the space. Bitcoin's momentum gauge sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend. Traders are watching the first floor just below the price as the line buyers must hold. Bitcoin's November slide has turned into one of the harshest months in its history. Hougan warned the industry may stay stuck in a long, quiet slump. The timing matters for holders. Rate worries, miner selling and political setbacks are hitting at once, and crypto stocks are falling with the coin. Traders now want to know whether this exhaustion marks a bottom or a pause before another leg lower. November Sell-Off Ranks Among Bitcoin's Worst on Record Bitcoin fell as low as $64,000 on Monday before trimming some of the loss. The slide leaves the coin down nearly 16% in November, its second-worst start to a month since 2016. Only November 2022, when the FTX exchange collapsed, was worse. The damage runs deeper over the year. Bitcoin is down 25% year to date, its third-worst showing through mid-November in a decade, behind only the 2018 and 2022 bear markets. Several headwinds hit at once. Traders expect tighter Federal Reserve policy. Public miners sped up their bitcoin sales in the first half, according to Needham & Co. A less friendly Democratic majority emerged after the midterms, and regulatory legislation failed. Binance also suffered the biggest hack on record last month. Shares of crypto companies followed the coin lower Monday morning. Robinhood lost 3% and Circle dropped 4%. Coinbase and Strategy each fell 5%. Hougan compared the mood to an earlier downturn. "Crypto is giving mid-2018 vibes, when the space was exhausted, and a lot of people gave up," he said. He warned the industry could "wander through the wilderness for a while." History offers a mixed signal. The last three bear markets bottomed about 12 to 13 months after their peaks. Bitcoin now sits just over 13 months past its October 2025 record, though nothing guarantees a rebound. Bitcoin Trades Far Beneath Both Long-Term Averages Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView Bitcoin trades in the mid-$60,000s, a long way under its two most-watched trend lines. The 50-day moving average, which tracks the average closing price over roughly the past ten weeks, sits near $77,000. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, sits near $76,000. Both lines now hang overhead and act as a ceiling. The gap to each is more than $10,000. That shows how far the price has fallen from where most recent buyers got in. The two averages also sit close together. The 50-day still holds just above the 200-day, but only by a thin margin. A shorter average that is rolling toward the longer one signals that the recent trend has turned against buyers. Selling has accelerated. Bitcoin dropped about 21% over the past 30 days and now trades at the bottom of that monthly range. About 14% of the decline came in the past week alone. Sellers pressed harder as the month went on. For bulls, a return to the averages is a distant target. Bitcoin would need to climb nearly a fifth just to touch them. Oversold Does Not Yet Mean Turning Bitcoin's daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 22. Readings below 30 count as oversold. That means sellers have pushed the price down faster than usual, and the market is stretched. Stretched markets often snap back. Such readings have frequently come before short relief rallies, as late sellers run out of coins to dump. Other signals still point the wrong way. The MACD, a tool that compares short and longer price trends, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downward momentum has not faded. Trend strength also shows a real move, and sellers are leading it. Together those readings describe exhaustion with no turn yet. Traders will want to see momentum cross back up before treating any rally as more than a pause. Where Buyers Must Make Their Stand The first floor sits near $62,000, just under where Bitcoin trades now. Buyers stepped in around that zone during Monday's drop, and the daily chart marks it as the nearest line to defend. Losing that level opens the way to the next support near $59,000. A break there would push the drawdown into fresh lows for this cycle and deepen the bear-market comparisons Hougan raised. Overhead, the first resistance stands near $75,000. That level sits just below the cluster formed by the two moving averages, so any rally would meet sellers in a crowded zone. The bigger test lies around $80,000. A clean move above it would put Bitcoin back over both averages. That would be the first real sign the wilderness phase is ending. Two Paths for the Next Three Days Bullish: Bitcoin holds the first floor and momentum starts to turn up. That would let the oversold bounce stretch toward the first resistance. A close below the deeper support would cancel this view. Bearish: A daily close under the first floor hands control to sellers. The next support then becomes the target. A recovery back above the first resistance would undo the bearish case and trap late sellers. Exhaustion Without Capitulation Yet Bitcoin looks stretched after weeks of heavy selling. For now, waiting for momentum to turn makes more sense than guessing the low. Hougan's warning fits that slower path. The risks remain sharp. A hawkish Fed surprise or fresh regulatory setback could push prices through the nearby floors fast. Oversold markets can stay oversold longer than buyers expect. title: Bitcoin Miners Hijacked as Attackers Redirect BTC Through Luxor Breach
tags: Bitcoin News|Bitcoin Miners|bitcoin miners hijacked|BTC miners|luxor software breach
body: Bitcoin miners hijacked as mining infrastructure provider Luxor has confirmed a security breach involving its Commander management software, which allowed attackers to redirect computing power from more than a dozen customer accounts to another mining pool and change the addresses receiving their rewards. The incident left affected miners paying electricity costs while their machines continued working for someone else’s benefit. Luxor said it detected the unauthorized activity on November 14, patched the software within two hours, and began restoring the original mining configurations. The company has also promised to reimburse affected customers in full. Attackers Exploit Luxor Commander to Redirect Mining Rewards The breach involved Commander, Luxor’s mining-management platform, which allows operators to monitor mining equipment and remotely adjust its settings. Attackers used unauthorized access to change the mining pool configurations of affected machines and redirect their payout addresses. Instead of sending their computing power to the pools selected by their owners, the machines were pointed toward OCEAN, a Bitcoin mining pool where participants combine their hashrate and receive rewards based on their contributed work. This type of attack does not require criminals to physically access mining equipment or steal Bitcoin directly from users’ wallets. By changing the pool and payout settings, attackers can redirect the revenue generated by mining machines while their legitimate owners continue covering electricity and operating expenses. The company also clarified that the incident was isolated to Commander. Its Luxor Pool and LuxOS services were not affected, and it reported no evidence that customer data had been leaked or extracted. Bitcoin Rewards Worth $15,700 Sent to Attacker-Controlled Address Blockchain activity indicates that the attackers managed to receive actual mining rewards during the incident. An address initially identified by mining host CoreX Hosting received three Bitcoin block-reward payments totaling approximately 0.243 BTC. At the time of reporting, the amount was valued at roughly $15,700. OCEAN’s payout mechanism helps explain why rewards can arrive even after mining machines have stopped contributing. Its system allows previously submitted mining work to remain eligible for a share of subsequent block rewards over a rolling period. Consequently, payments can reach an address after the affected machines have already been returned to their original configurations. The full financial impact remains unclear, and the identified payments do not establish the total amount of revenue diverted during the incident. Reports Suggest 64,000 Mining Machines Were Redirected The incident may have affected considerably more computing power than the number of customer accounts confirmed by Luxor. Mining operators first raised concerns after noticing unauthorized changes to their equipment’s pool settings. CoreX Hosting reportedly identified the suspicious activity and helped alert other affected operators. The redirected hashrate subsequently dropped sharply, with reports indicating that it had fallen to approximately 100 petahashes per second. This suggested that most of the affected computing power had been restored or was no longer contributing to the suspicious pool. Luxor CEO Warns of Increasing AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Luxor CEO Nick Hansen described the intrusion as involving a sophisticated AI-enabled attack, warning that cryptocurrency businesses are facing increasingly advanced cybersecurity threats. However, he did not explain precisely how artificial intelligence was used in the breach or disclose how the attackers initially gained access to Commander. Hansen also said Luxor had paused much of its new feature development to focus on strengthening its security infrastructure. The company has reportedly acquired dedicated GPUs to run its own AI models for defensive security testing. The warning comes amid growing concerns about the use of artificial intelligence in cyberattacks targeting cryptocurrency companies and blockchain infrastructure providers. AI tools can potentially help attackers identify vulnerabilities and automate parts of the exploitation process, although the specific role of AI in this incident has not been independently established. Mining Security Concerns Grow After Luxor Breach The incident highlights a security risk that extends beyond cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet providers. Mining management platforms also control access to valuable infrastructure and determine where the rewards generated by computing power are sent. Even without directly stealing equipment or accessing miners’ existing Bitcoin balances, attackers who gain control of mining configurations can redirect future earnings and leave operators responsible for the associated costs. Luxor’s compensation commitment addresses the immediate financial impact for affected customers, but the incident raises broader questions about access controls, monitoring systems, and the security of remotely managed mining operations. Will Luxor’s promise to fully reimburse affected customers be enough to restore confidence in its mining management software?

title: Cardano Voters Reject 22,000,000 ADA Copper Reserve
body: Cardano’s 22 million ADA copper reserve proposal expired with 126 DReps against and five in favor. Explicit opposition outweighed support by roughly 143 to 1. Cardano ’s delegated representatives overwhelmingly opposed a proposal to spend 22 million ADA from the treasury to buy and tokenize physical copper. Toto Finance’s request expired on November 15 with 126 representatives voting against it, five in favor and eight abstaining. The treasury released no funds under the proposal. The gap was wider when measured by voting power. Representatives who explicitly voted no accounted for 2.86 billion ADA in delegated stake, compared with 20.02 million ADA behind the yes votes. That put opposition at roughly 143 ADA for every 1 ADA in favor, even before counting stake that sat out the vote. Why the Final Tally Shows 3.93 Billion ADA Against Cardano weights these votes by the amount of ADA delegated to each representative, or DRep. Under the rules for this treasury withdrawal, the proposal needed support from 67% of the stake included in the approval calculation. It received 0.51% by the time voting expired at 21:44 UTC on November 15. Final voting category Delegated stake Explicit yes 20.02 million ADA Explicit no 2.86 billion ADA Automatic no-confidence stake 131.29 million ADA Eligible stake that did not vote 936.13 million ADA The last three categories counted toward the 3.93 billion ADA on the no side of the approval calculation. This explains why the official result reads 99.49% no even though only 2.86 billion ADA carried an explicit no vote. The 143-to-1 comparison uses only stake whose representatives chose a side. The proposal also needed five of Cardano’s seven Constitutional Committee members to attest that it complied with the constitution. Three members judged it unconstitutional, and the other four submitted no vote. Those constitutional objections had surfaced in October , more than two weeks before the deadline. What the Treasury Would Have Bought Toto Finance submitted the request on October 15. The company proposed using the ADA to purchase independently verified COMEX Grade 1 copper cathodes held in a COMEX-approved U.S. warehouse. It would tokenize the copper as CuTT and serve as the recipient and administrator of the treasury funds. Published voting explanations identify two objections. One representative questioned giving a single key control over the address receiving all 22 million ADA. Another acknowledged the potential for real-world assets on Cardano but argued that the copper purchase exposed the treasury to commodity prices and execution risks. Even if the metal remained safely warehoused, recovering the original amount of ADA would depend in part on how copper performed relative to ADA. Cardano has separately advanced standards for tokenized shares . The decision here concerned who would finance the underlying asset. Toto Finance asked the network treasury to put up the purchase money and bear the investment risk. Only five DReps backed those terms.

title: Tesla to Invest $3.3B in Berlin Gigafactory as Cybercab Production Targets 2029
body: Key takeaways Tesla announces $3.3 billion Berlin factory expansion Cybercab production in Germany targets 2029 launch New facility could eventually produce one million robotaxis Tesla ( NASDAQ: TSLA ) plans to invest €3 billion ($3.3 billion) in expanding its Berlin Gigafactory, preparing to manufacture autonomous Cybercab vehicles in Germany beginning in 2029 as Elon Musk accelerates the company's transition toward robotaxi production. The November 16 announcement outlines a new production facility in Grünheide, Brandenburg, designed to eventually accommodate annual output of up to one million Cybercabs. Tesla expects construction to begin in the first half of 2027, subject to permitting. The investment adds another dimension to Tesla's shift toward robotaxis , which has increasingly shaped investor expectations for the electric vehicle maker. Tesla Plans $3.3B Gigafactory Berlin Expansion According to Tesla's announcement reported by German newspaper Tagesspiegel, the company intends to construct an additional manufacturing building at its only European vehicle factory. The €3 billion investment will also support ancillary facilities, including wastewater treatment infrastructure required for the expansion. Tesla plans to submit its construction permit application before the end of 2026, with building work targeted for the first half of 2027 and Cybercab manufacturing scheduled to begin in 2029. The project is expected to create new employment opportunities, with Tesla initially seeking several hundred workers for construction and manufacturing planning. The expansion follows improved production at Grünheide. Tesla's official third-quarter update confirmed record output at Gigafactory Berlin, which currently manufactures Model Y vehicles. Berlin Cybercab Capacity Could Exceed Tesla's Texas Operations The proposed European facility represents a major increase in Tesla's potential robotaxi manufacturing capacity. Tesla's third-quarter shareholder update listed installed annual Cybercab manufacturing capacity exceeding 125,000 vehicles at Gigafactory Texas, where production is already underway. By comparison, the planned Berlin complex could eventually accommodate up to one million Cybercabs annually, roughly eight times the Texas facility's stated minimum installed capacity. However, the figure represents a long-term production objective, not guaranteed output when the German facility opens in 2029. Tesla's emphasis on autonomous transportation has already influenced TSLA stock valuation , with investors increasingly assessing future robotaxi revenue alongside conventional vehicle deliveries. What Does the Investment Mean for TSLA Stock? Tesla shares closed November 13 at $390.22, down 1.82% for the session, before the Berlin announcement. The November 16 expansion provides another potential long-term growth catalyst, although its immediate contribution to Tesla's earnings remains uncertain. The announcement comes as Tesla continues expanding autonomous driving services while investing heavily in manufacturing and battery infrastructure. Its robotaxi growth ambitions remain dependent on regulatory approvals, manufacturing execution and consumer adoption. The company must also manage the financial demands of expanding several production programs simultaneously, a challenge reflected in earlier Tesla stock forecasts .

title: Vitalik Buterin Backs Faster Route to Quantum-Safe Ethereum With New Proposal
tags: News|ethereum safety|new proposal|quantum safe|quantum safe ethereum|vitalik buterin
body: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has thrown his support behind leanPCS, a cryptographic technique that could help the blockchain prepare for future quantum computing threats without significantly increasing transaction costs or on-chain data requirements. Buterin’s change of position centers on EIP-8288, a draft proposal designed to combine large digital signatures and cryptographic proofs into a shared mathematical proof. Instead of requiring Ethereum to store every quantum-resistant signature individually, the approach would allow computers to aggregate verification data before transactions are added to the blockchain. I n a November 16 post on X, Buterin described his change of view, writing that he had gone from considering leanPCS “total bull” to becoming “a total bull” on the approach. The proposal addresses one of Ethereum’s biggest potential challenges in preparing for quantum-resistant cryptography: the significantly larger size of the signatures and proofs that would replace today’s cryptographic standards. Buterin Changes His Position on leanPCS as Ethereum Advances Quantum Defenses Buterin’s endorsement reflects growing confidence in a method that could make Ethereum’s transition toward quantum resistance more practical. Current Ethereum signatures typically occupy around 65 bytes. By comparison, some quantum-resistant alternatives could require between 1,000 and 6,000 bytes, according to Buterin. Certain cryptographic proofs used by privacy applications could also expand from a few hundred bytes to approximately 128 kilobytes. Storing this additional information directly on Ethereum would consume considerably more block space. That could increase the cost of transactions and make it more expensive for users to interact with decentralized applications. The approach relies on polynomial commitment schemes, mathematical tools used in cryptographic proof systems. By standardizing a shared verification component, different proof systems could use the same underlying mechanism without requiring developers to adopt an identical architecture. Buterin believes this could provide Ethereum with a faster route toward supporting quantum-resistant accounts and more advanced cryptographic applications. EIP-8288 Could Combine Thousands of Signatures Into One Proof Under the design, users would continue submitting signatures or cryptographic proofs to demonstrate that transactions and other operations are valid. However, rather than storing every large signature individually, network participants could combine multiple verification results into aggregated proofs. Ethereum would only need to retain the transaction instructions and sufficient information to verify the aggregated result. The full collection of bulky signatures and proofs would not need to be permanently stored on-chain. The benefits could also extend beyond wallet security. Privacy applications that rely on zero-knowledge proofs could use the same approach to demonstrate that transactions follow the required rules without revealing sensitive information. By reducing the amount of data that needs to be recorded individually, proof aggregation could make more advanced cryptographic features practical without placing the entire storage burden on Ethereum users. Three Approaches Considered for Ethereum’s Quantum-Safe Transition EIP-8288 outlines three possible approaches to handling the larger signatures and proofs required by quantum-resistant systems. The first, leanSPHINCS, is the most specialized option. It would support a particular family of hash-based quantum-resistant signatures, offering a relatively straightforward path toward protecting Ethereum accounts. However, its functionality would be limited to that signature system. At the other end of the spectrum is leanSTARK, a more general approach that could support different signature schemes, privacy applications, and more complex verification processes. Its implementation would require Ethereum developers to agree on a new programming language for the programs being verified. That decision could represent a substantial architectural change for Ethereum, potentially extending beyond its existing Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) framework. This is the approach Buterin now favors, arguing that it could be introduced considerably sooner. The broader leanSTARK framework could potentially follow later, allowing Ethereum to expand its cryptographic capabilities over time. Buterin described the opportunity as a route toward a “cryptographic proof singularity” much sooner than developers had previously expected. Ethereum’s Quantum-Security Roadmap Gains Momentum Buterin’s latest endorsement comes as Ethereum developers increasingly prioritize protection against potential quantum computing threats. The Ethereum Foundation established a dedicated post-quantum research team earlier in 2026, while developers have been exploring changes to account authentication, validator keys, and privacy-related cryptography. EIP-8288 could become an important component of this broader effort by addressing the additional data and verification costs associated with quantum-resistant systems. However, the proposal remains a draft, and its reference implementation is unfinished. Buterin’s support does not mean that leanPCS has been approved for deployment or assigned a mainnet activation date. If the approach proves practical, it could help the network adopt stronger cryptographic protections while limiting the impact on transaction fees and blockchain storage requirements. title: Luxor confirms Commander breach after 13 EH/s diverted
body: BitcoinWorld Luxor confirms Commander breach after 13 EH/s diverted Bitcoin mining technology firm Luxor said its Commander mining-management platform was breached, allowing an unauthorized redirect of hashrate across more than a dozen client accounts. The company disclosed the incident after mining infrastructure provider CoreX Hosting raised the alarm on Nov. 15 that equipment was being pointed at the OCEAN pool with rewards assigned to a single Bitcoin address, Cryptoslate reported . Luxor confirmed that an unauthorized redirect of hashrate was made through its Commander platform over a limited window, affecting more than a dozen client accounts. The company patched the platform within two hours and has promised to compensate affected customers, but has not confirmed the reported scale of the diversion. Key facts CoreX Hosting flagged the redirect on Nov. 15, naming the Bitcoin address bc1qphuk…pcddrr as the payout destination. GalaxyMind estimated that about 64,000 machines and 13 EH/s were redirected from around 8 p.m. Central Time on Nov. 14, with CoinSpect putting the computing power at roughly 1.5% of Bitcoin’s global hashrate. OCEAN data shows three payments totaling 0.24308905 BTC to the named address between Nov. 15 and Nov. 16, including 0.08088977 BTC in block 975995. Luxor CEO Nick Hansen blamed a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector” and said the attack began around 6 p.m. Pacific time on Nov. 14. CoreX said it restored affected miners, and later declared the incident over after computing power tied to the suspicious address fell to about 100 PH/s. How the diversion was spotted and what the blockchain shows CoreX’s alert at 03:08 GMT on Nov. 15 named the destination address. At 17:25 GMT, mempool.space recorded a confirmed transaction funding that address with 8,088,977 satoshis — 0.08088977 BTC — with no recorded spending. That output was part of the coinbase transaction in block 975995, timestamped 17:22:50 GMT on Nov. 15 and labelled OCEAN by mempool.space. The record establishes that a reported destination became a recorded reward recipient. It does not establish who controls the address, nor prove which incident shares generated the payment. OCEAN’s TIDES reward system lets previously submitted work qualify for payments from later blocks, so rewards can keep arriving after hashing stops. Eligibility does not guarantee another payment. CoreX said it believed it had isolated the program behind the unauthorized changes. It reported restoring machines to their original configurations, then declared the episode closed once the suspicious address’s associated hashrate collapsed. Luxor’s account: two-hour patch and a promise to pay Luxor said its own monitoring caught the redirect and that affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window. The firm stated no data was leaked or exfiltrated, patched Commander within two hours, and began returning machines to their original pools. It pledged full compensation for the redirected computing power. Hansen apologised to affected customers and warned that crypto businesses face a rising tide of automated attacks, saying abliterated models run around the clock probing every exposed surface and expand almost instantly through any weakness. He said Luxor had bought dedicated GPUs to run its own modified models for defensive testing and suspended much of its new feature development to harden infrastructure. Luxor has not disclosed how Commander was compromised and has not confirmed GalaxyMind’s estimates of machine count or hashrate. Why it matters The incident targeted the management layer rather than the mining hardware itself, which means an operator’s rigs can work and burn power while earnings flow somewhere else — a cost hit that shows up only after payouts diverge. Luxor’s promise of compensation covers its own clients, but the breach raises a question every hosting customer faces: who holds the authority to change pool settings, and how quickly would an unauthorised change be noticed? Hansen’s warning also frames this as a security-cost problem for the sector, with one vendor diverting engineering resources from product work into defensive hardening. What to watch Luxor has committed to a full post-mortem, which should establish the entry point, the true scale of the disruption and whether all the reported computing power ran through its compromised platform. Watch whether those findings reconcile with GalaxyMind’s 64,000-machine estimate. Frequently Asked Questions How much hashrate was affected by the Luxor Commander incident? Luxor has not confirmed the scale. GalaxyMind estimated that roughly 64,000 machines and 13 EH/s were redirected, and CoinSpect said that represented about 1.5% of Bitcoin’s global hashrate. What did Luxor say caused the breach? Luxor CEO Nick Hansen attributed the compromise to what he called a sophisticated AI-enabled vector and said the attack started around 6 p.m. Pacific time on Nov. 14. The precise entry point has not been disclosed. Did the attackers receive Bitcoin rewards? Yes. OCEAN data shows three payments totaling 0.24308905 BTC to the address named in CoreX’s alert between Nov. 15 and Nov. 16, including 0.08088977 BTC in block 975995. Was customer data taken from Luxor’s systems? Luxor stated that no data was leaked or exfiltrated from its systems during the incident. What should miners take away from this incident? Because redirected machines kept consuming electricity while rewards went elsewhere, operators should review who can change pool configuration on their equipment and monitor payout addresses for unexpected edits. title: Harvard, Dartmouth Hold Bitcoin ETF Stakes Steady as IBIT Gains 42%
body: BitcoinWorld Harvard, Dartmouth Hold Bitcoin ETF Stakes Steady as IBIT Gains 42% Harvard University reported 3.04 million shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) in its latest SEC Form 13F filing , a position worth about $144.1 million at the end of September 2026. Dartmouth College disclosed 201,531 IBIT shares valued at $9.5 million in the same filing period, Cointelegraph reported . Harvard kept its IBIT share count at 3.04 million and Dartmouth at 201,531 through the end of Q3 2026, according to SEC 13F filings. The unchanged positions came as BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF gained about 42% and Bitcoin rose nearly 43% during the quarter. Key facts Harvard reported 3.04 million IBIT shares, valued at roughly $144.1 million at the end of September 2026. Dartmouth reported 201,531 IBIT shares, valued at about $9.5 million. IBIT gained about 42% in Q3 2026, while Bitcoin rose nearly 43% — the strongest quarterly gains for both through September. Harvard has reported the same IBIT share count since the end of March 2026, after cutting its holdings by 43% in Q1 and 21% in Q4 2025. Dartmouth has reported the same 201,531 shares since first disclosing its Bitcoin ETF position in Q4 2025. Harvard shifts toward gold while holding Bitcoin steady While Harvard’s Bitcoin ETF position stayed flat, its gold exposure changed sharply. The university’s share count in State Street’s SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) rose nearly 20-fold in Q3, to 1.16 million shares from 58,862, worth $442.2 million at the end of September. At Harvard, the gold ETF position now holds a larger reported dollar value than its IBIT stake. That shift occurred in the same quarter that IBIT posted its biggest gain of the year. Dartmouth also kept its other crypto-related ETF positions unchanged. It again reported 304,803 shares of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF and 178,148 shares of the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF, worth $4.9 million and $4.5 million respectively at quarter-end. Universities diverge from Wall Street in Q3 The steady university holdings contrasted with moves by major financial companies. Jane Street reduced its IBIT shares by 19% in Q3, while JPMorgan Chase increased the number of shares it held by 9.6%, according to their latest quarterly filings. The divergence suggests that endowments and trading firms are not moving in lockstep on Bitcoin ETF exposure. For the two universities, the filings show a quarter of no net change rather than either accumulating or exiting. Market snapshot As of November 16, 2026, at 15:18 UTC, Bitcoin traded at $65,257 (₹6,129,254), up 0.9% over 24 hours but down 13.4% over seven days, according to CoinPaprika data. Its market capitalization stood at $1.31 trillion, with 24-hour volume of $19.44 billion. Ether traded at $1,852 (₹173,946), up 2.4% in 24 hours and down 13.5% on the week. Why it matters 13F filings offer one of the few regular public windows into how large institutional investors treat crypto ETFs. Harvard’s flat IBIT position alongside a near-20-fold increase in gold ETF shares gives readers a concrete example of one endowment rebalancing toward traditional safe-haven assets while holding its Bitcoin exposure steady. For retail investors, the contrast among universities and trading firms is a reminder that institutional conviction on Bitcoin ETFs is not uniform. Cointelegraph reported that Harvard had trimmed its IBIT position in Q1 and Q4 2025 before holding steady in the two most recent quarters. What to watch The next round of SEC Form 13F filings, due for the fourth quarter of 2026, will show whether Harvard and Dartmouth maintain their current share counts or adjust them after Bitcoin’s recent price decline. Jane Street’s and JPMorgan’s Q4 filings will also indicate whether the divergence in their IBIT positions continues. title: Trump Faces Pressure to Tighten Nvidia Chip Restrictions Ahead of Xi Summit
body: Key takeaways Trump faces bipartisan pressure over Nvidia chip exports US introduces new restrictions on overseas AI computing China technology tensions intensify before November 19 summit President Donald Trump faces growing pressure from U.S. lawmakers to tighten restrictions on Nvidia's advanced AI chips ahead of his November 19 meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as Washington moves to close potential loopholes in technology export controls. On November 15, the U.S. Commerce Department announced new restrictions targeting remote access to advanced American computing systems through overseas data centers. The move comes amid congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China business and questions about the enforcement of existing export rules. The dispute adds another challenge to the administration following the Nvidia chip export controversy , which has intensified pressure on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. US Tightens AI Chip Controls Before Trump-Xi Summit According to the Bureau of Industry and Security , the newly issued interim final rule addresses arrangements that could allow restricted companies to access American AI computing infrastructure remotely. Existing export controls primarily restrict shipments of advanced chips and computing systems. However, companies can potentially obtain access to similar computing capabilities through cloud infrastructure located outside restricted countries. The new rule aims to address that distinction by strengthening oversight of remote computing arrangements involving third-country data centers. The restrictions could affect cloud infrastructure providers operating in countries such as Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. The issue builds on previous concerns surrounding Nvidia's overseas data center partners , which have faced growing scrutiny over Chinese access to AI computing services. Congress Demands Stronger Nvidia Export Enforcement The regulatory announcement follows renewed pressure from both Democratic and Republican lawmakers. In a November 9 statement , Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks called for stronger restrictions on advanced chip exports and enforcement against potential diversion to China's military. The lawmakers also urged Congress to advance the AI Overwatch Act, which seeks to strengthen oversight of sensitive semiconductor technology. On November 11, Warren and Senator Chris Coons separately demanded that administration officials preserve records concerning Nvidia's exports, licensing decisions and reported national security concerns. The requests follow investigations that contributed to congressional scrutiny of Jensen Huang . Although some officials have criticized the administration's enforcement record, reports indicate Trump previously authorized restrictions targeting suspected chip diversion. The dispute therefore concerns implementation and the scope of future controls, rather than a confirmed presidential rejection of tighter rules. What Could the Restrictions Mean for Nvidia Stock? China remains a sensitive market for Nvidia, although the company's existing exposure to licensed advanced-chip sales is limited. Earlier disclosures showed that Nvidia's H200 sales to China represented less than 1% of data center revenue despite U.S. licensing approvals. Additional restrictions could complicate overseas cloud partnerships and licensing, although the financial impact remains uncertain. The development arrives immediately before Nvidia's November 17 earnings , when investors will assess its $108 billion revenue guidance and international business outlook.

title: Solana Officially Exits Beta After Six Years With New Network Versioning System
tags: News|new network system|solana|Solana Blockchain|Solana Foundation|solana mainnet beta
body: Solana officially exits “mainnet beta” label it carried for more than six years, marking a new milestone in the blockchain’s development since its launch in March 2020. The network will now operate under the Solana Mainnet name, while a new shared protocol designation, Solana 1.0, will provide a common reference for its underlying rules. The Solana Foundation announced the change on November 16, explaining that the beta label no longer reflected the network’s current status. Solana has been processing live transactions and supporting applications since its genesis block, making the designation increasingly outdated. The update does not introduce an immediate change for users. SOL balances, wallets, accounts, applications, and transaction histories will remain unaffected, and no action is required from token holders. Solana Replaces Mainnet Beta With Solana 1.0 The removal of the beta designation represents a change in how Solana identifies its network rather than a new blockchain launch. Since March 2020, the network has operated under the name Solana Mainnet Beta. The foundation said the label remained in place despite the blockchain functioning as a live production network throughout its development. Under the new system, the blockchain will simply be referred to as Solana Mainnet. Solana 1.0 will serve as a shared version number describing the network’s protocol rules. This distinction is important because Solana relies on different validator software implementations, each with its own development schedule and version numbers. Previously, these individual releases could make it harder for developers and infrastructure operators to identify which network rules were supported across different clients. The new protocol version provides a common reference point, allowing operators to track network changes without relying on the release number of a particular software implementation. Alpenglow and Firedancer Help Mark Solana’s Progress The decision to retire the beta label follows several infrastructure improvements intended to strengthen Solana’s performance and reliability. One of the most significant developments is Alpenglow, a consensus upgrade activated on the network in October. The upgrade changes how validators reach agreement and aims to reduce transaction finality to approximately 150 milliseconds, compared with the previous 12.8 seconds. Transaction finality refers to the point at which the network considers a transaction settled. Faster finality can improve the experience for applications that depend on rapid confirmations, including trading platforms and other real-time services. Another important development is Firedancer, an independently developed validator client created by Jump Crypto. It provides an alternative to Agave, the network’s existing client implementation. Running multiple independent clients can improve network resilience by reducing reliance on a single codebase. If one implementation experiences a software issue, the presence of another can help limit the potential impact on the broader network. Solana Ecosystem Holds Billions in DeFi and Stablecoins Solana’s infrastructure developments come as the network maintains significant activity across decentralized finance and digital asset markets. According to DefiLlama figures, approximately $4.66 billion was deposited in Solana-based decentralized finance applications. The network also held around $14 billion in circulating stablecoins. Solana-based decentralized exchanges processed approximately $1.28 billion in trading volume over the 24 hours preceding the report. These figures highlight the scale of the ecosystem operating on the blockchain, which now supports a broad range of financial applications and digital assets. Despite the network’s milestone, SOL was trading near $70 at the time of the report, down approximately 3% over 24 hours. The naming change itself does not introduce any direct improvement to transaction costs or speed, meaning the token’s market performance will continue to depend on broader market conditions and developments across the ecosystem. What Solana’s Move Beyond Beta Means for Users and Developers Solana’s decision to retire the beta label marks a symbolic milestone, but the introduction of shared protocol versioning also has practical implications for the network’s technical development. For everyday users, the transition requires no action. Existing SOL holdings, accounts, applications, and transaction records will remain exactly as they were. Developers and infrastructure operators, however, will need to pay attention to the new versioning system. Validator and RPC operators should check which Agave and Firedancer releases support each protocol rollout, while application developers will need to continue monitoring relevant software and infrastructure updates. The change also reflects Solana’s growing emphasis on independent client implementations and coordinated network upgrades. As the ecosystem expands, having a shared protocol reference could make it easier for different development teams to work toward the same technical standards. After more than six years under the mainnet beta designation, Solana is now presenting itself as a mature production network. Whether its latest infrastructure improvements translate into sustained growth will depend on continued adoption, developer activity, and the network’s ability to maintain reliability as usage increases. Will upgrades such as Alpenglow and Firedancer help Solana strengthen its position against competing blockchain networks?
